## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->
<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis-head: e06aad70b39fa35546bcf1c8149ca056d9865469 -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #447 is the first dispatch-intent slice from #446, under parent issue #443. It tightens bare `@sepo-agent` mention triage so clear add/fix/change requests can infer an implementation route, while planning or question-shaped requests stay in `answer`. It preserves the existing approval gate for triaged write routes and keeps explicit slash-command behavior unchanged. The PR is stacked on #444 and only changes the dispatch prompt plus focused triage prompt tests.

## Review
Overall, the PR is narrow and aligned with the requested UX change. The only unresolved issue is a small prompt consistency problem that slightly weakens the stated “clear add asks” behavior; it is not blocking, but it is concrete and easy to fix.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `"add"` keyword narrowed to `"please add"` | WARNING | The prompt now lists `"please add"` while leaving `"change"` as a bare verb, even though both are disambiguated by the new question/planning rules. This can make plain imperatives like `@sepo-agent add error handling here` lean on the weaker general rule instead of the keyword list. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review passed with no rubric-specific blocking or warning findings.
- Codex review reported SHIP; Claude review raised the single warning above.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis.
- Posted one new inline comment on `.github/prompts/agent-dispatch.md` line 39: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/447#discussion_r3504553339
- No comments were minimized, no replies were added, and no threads were resolved.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>"add" keyword narrowed to "please add"</summary>

**Cause:** The implement keyword examples changed from `"add"` to `"please add"`, while `"change"` remains a bare verb. The new prompt already covers `can we` / `should we` / question-shaped cases, including `can we add ...?`, so narrowing only `add` is inconsistent with the PR’s stated goal.

**Candidate solutions:** Restore `"add"` in the keyword list, or list both `"add"` and `"please add"`. The existing `please add` test still covers the implement example, so no test change appears required.

**Comments:** This is a reviewer disagreement: Claude flagged it as a warning, while Codex and rubrics review found no actionable issues. The failure mode is safe but slightly under-routes clear bare `add` imperatives.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: The remaining issue is a concrete one-line prompt consistency fix that is safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
MINOR_ISSUES

## Action Items
- [ ] Restore `"add"` to the implement keyword list, or list both `"add"` and `"please add"` to keep clear bare add requests aligned with the dispatch-intent goal.
